tickerNote: US closes Fri 6 Nov · India: Muhurat session, Sun 8 Nov

lead.headline: AI Rout Rattles Wall Street as Strong Jobs Data Steadies the Week's Close
lead.deck: Chip stocks suffered their sharpest fall since 2020 before a Friday rebound; the Nasdaq still ended the week down 3.4%.
body: A sudden loss of faith in the artificial-intelligence trade dominated the week. On Thursday the semiconductor index fell as much as 11% intraday, its steepest drop since March 2020, and the Nasdaq Composite slid into correction territory. Midterm wins by Democratic candidates critical of AI added to doubts about how long the boom can run.
Friday brought partial relief. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq gained 1.1%, while the Dow slipped 0.5%. For the week, the S&P 500 lost 2.7% and the Nasdaq 3.4%.

The economy gave buyers a reason to return: employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above the roughly 59,000 forecast, and unemployment held at 4.1%. A stronger labour market eases recession fears but may complicate the case for further rate cuts.

Hedge funds felt the turn sharply. Managers sold about $20 billion of tech stocks over two weeks, unwinding nearly all the net AI buying they had done since early 2025, according to Goldman Sachs data.

top: US stocks closed a bruising week lower despite Friday's bounce: S&P 500 −2.7%, Nasdaq −3.4%.
Fox completed its $22 billion takeover of Roku, months ahead of the original schedule.
SEBI cleared Razorpay's IPO, which would value the payments company near ₹47,000 crore.
Jewellery brand GIVA raised $103 million, leading a $255 million week for Indian startups.
Walleye Capital is restructuring its stock-picking unit after its worst month since 2020.

items.headline: US Payrolls Beat Forecasts
items.body: October hiring came in well above the 59,000 economists expected, steadying markets after Thursday's slide.

items.headline: Quiet Muhurat Session in Mumbai
items.body: Benchmarks finished the Diwali special session slightly lower while mid- and small-caps rose. Power and metals drew buyers; IT and state-run banks were sold.

items.headline: Asian Tech Hubs Hit Hard
items.body: Japanese and South Korean shares fell sharply alongside Thursday's US chip selloff.

items.headline: Rupee Remains Weak
items.body: The rupee traded around 93.9 to the dollar during the weekend session.

items.headline: Chipmakers Lead the AI Unwind
items.body: Semiconductor names took the heaviest losses as funds cut crowded AI positions.

items.headline: Tata Steel Posts Strong Quarter
items.body: Q2 FY27 consolidated profit rose to ₹3,666 crore on 11.5% revenue growth; the stock was among Sunday's top gainers.

items.headline: Data Patterns Sales Slump
items.body: The defence electronics maker's quarterly revenue more than halved, though margins improved.

items.headline: Winners and Laggards on Dalal Street
items.body: Sun Pharma and Maruti Suzuki gained; Trent, Infosys and Bharti Airtel were the main drags. Adani Ports and Eternal touched 52-week highs.

items.headline: Fox Completes Roku Takeover
items.body: The deal, first expected to close in 2027, gives Fox direct reach into more than 100 million streaming households and makes it the third-largest US TV business by viewership.

items.headline: Influence Media Buys Anthem Catalogs
items.body: The music investor completed its purchase of Anthem Entertainment's song catalogs.

items.headline: Blue Ashva Exits iD Fresh Food
items.body: The fund sold its entire stake in the packaged-food brand to three new investors.

items.headline: Nuuk Seeks ₹100 Crore
items.body: The D2C home-appliance brand is reportedly raising from Wipro Consumer Care Ventures and RPSG Capital Ventures.

items.headline: Walleye Overhauls Equity Unit
items.body: The $17 billion firm is parting with leadership and much of its long-short stock team, shifting stock picking to outside managers.

items.headline: Engineers Gate Trims a Team
items.body: The quant firm is reportedly letting go most of its 'synthesis' stock group.

items.headline: Big Names Lose Ground in October
items.body: Marshall Wace, Millennium, ExodusPoint and North Rock all finished the month in the red.

items.headline: Arini Sells Positions
items.body: The credit-focused fund's losses deepened and it sold some holdings, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: Razorpay Gets IPO Nod
items.body: SEBI approved the listing, expected between January and March 2027.

items.headline: Coca-Cola's Indian Bottler Files for IPO
items.body: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings submitted draft papers for an offer-for-sale.

items.headline: GIVA Raises a Large Round
items.body: Multiples Alternate Asset Management led the investment in the silver and demi-fine jewellery brand, the week's biggest Indian deal.

items.headline: Indian Startup Funding Nearly Doubles
items.body: Funding rose 96% week on week; EloElo Group added an $80 million Series C backed by NBCUniversal.
